source.title: What Lies Beneath
source.summary: The resource curse, Dutch disease, critical minerals, and the Islamic concept of communal resource ownership.
source.author: Islamic Economics
source.body_text: Countries that discover oil or minerals often end up worse off, not better. The resource curse is one of the most robust findings in development economics: resource wealth weakens institutions, concentrates power, and crowds out productive sectors through Dutch disease. This episode covers the mechanism, the evidence, and the exceptions (Norway, Botswana). Then it turns to Islamic resource economics: the fay' principle that communal resources belong to the community, the hima system of protected commons, and how sovereign wealth funds (particularly the Gulf model) represent a partial modern application. Pakistan's critical minerals reserves make this directly relevant. The honest assessment: Islamic principles point in the right direction, but no Muslim-majority resource economy has fully solved the institutional challenge.
